claims_boundary: Public proposals are tracked by maturity and dependency. Draft specifications and reference implementations are not consensus deployment, and a rescue design that depends on PQ authorization is not operational until a suitable PQ authorization/output path is active.

components.name: SHRINCS
components.claims_note: Executable draft specification with a demonstration Python implementation. The draft explicitly marks the security proof and comprehensive test vectors as TODO and warns that the reference implementation is non-constant-time and not for production.

components.name: DropKick
components.claims_note: Commit/reveal rescue design for legacy coins. Its author explicitly states that on-chain PQ signatures/addresses are a prerequisite, so it cannot independently make Bitcoin PQ-ready.

components.name: BIP-361
components.claims_note: Draft legacy-signature sunset framework. The BIP itself requires a future post-quantum signature BIP, so its migration phases are dependency-blocked until a PQ output/signature mechanism exists.

blocking_gaps: SHRINCS security proof is not complete in the public draft.
Comprehensive SHRINCS test vectors are not complete.
No production Bitcoin implementation is represented by the draft reference code.
No PQ authorization/output mechanism represented here is consensus-active.
DropKick requires an already-functioning PQ authorization/output destination.
BIP-361 requires a future PQ signature BIP and remains Draft.
